newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end range-bound session slightly down.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end range-bound session slightly down.

text.p: Dutch shares ended barely changed from their opening levels on Thursday after a day's range-bound trading in negative territory.
The AEX blue chip index ended the day down 2.27 points at 687.22 from Wednesday's record close, but off its low of 684.09. The index opened at 687.09.
Dealers said the day's trade had been overshadowed by German jobless figures which rose to a post-war record in January.
But they said that nevertheless Amsterdam had largely shrugged off Wall Street's lower overnight close and its opening slip on Thursday, helped by a firm dollar and pound sterling.
"Wednesday's Wall Street fall was exaggerated," one dealer said. The New York Stock Exchange opened lower on Thursday, but swung into the black before Amsterdam trading ended.
A lack of fresh corporate news made for muted trade, with AEX component stocks drifting marginally lower across the board.
Exceptions were foods group Nutricia, which surged 5.80 or 2.19 percent to 270.30 on rumours of a foreign broker upgrade saying the stock had upward potential to 400 guilders.
KLM Royal Dutch Airlines outpaced the market's fall, shedding 2.30 guilders to 53.30 after Wednesday's rally, which dealers ascribed to short-covering.
Also hurrying down ahead of the market was Philips, which lost 1.50 guilders to 74.40 in brisk trade on nervousness before its full-year results due to be released next Thursday.

Stocks bucking the downtrend included brewer Heineken, newly perceived as lagging the market's rise of recent months on the back of rumours that its results due next month would be better than forecast. Heineken shares added 2.20 to close at 309.20.

Also up was Akzo, due to publish full-year results in a fortnight's time. The chemicals group gained 2.90 to 271.30. Earlier today its pharmaceuticals arm vowed to fight ongoing German restrictions on its best-seller oral contraceptives. REUTER/lvl
